To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Na(+)/H(+) exchanger in synaptosomes can be regulated by Cl(-) ions.
the Cl- concentration in the synaptosomal cytosol is about 50 mM and the Na+/H+ antiporter is responsible for most of the alkalinization observed upon removal of Cl-
1) the Na+/H+ antiporter is present in rat brain synapses; and 2) this transporter is coupled to Cl- transport.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of the Na+/H+ antiporter in the regulation of intracellular pH (pH(i)) in synaptosomes and in the regulation of synaptic transmission.
the role of the Na+/H+ antiport in the regulation of intracellular pH in synaptosomes.
the regulation of pH in brain cells, with a special emphasis on the regulation of intracellular pH (pHi) in synaptosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Na(+)/H(+) exchange is not the only way to control the pHi in synaptosomes.
the Na+/H+ antiporter in rat brain synapto-somes has a high affinity for Na+ and H+ and that the Na+/Cl- antiporter has a high affinity only for Cl-.
Cl- ions play an important role in the regulation of pH in brain synaptosomes, and that Cl- ions are involved in the Na+/H+ and Na+-HCO3- exchangers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Na+/H+ exchange in synaptosomes, as in other cell types, can be inhibited by DIDS and by the Cl- ionophore DMO.
the Na+/H+ antiporter is a key player in the regulation of pH in brain synaptosomes.
the Na+/H+ exchange system in synaptosomes can be regulated by Cl- and HCO3- ions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na+/H+ exchange in brain synaptosomes is not only coupled to Cl- but it is also regulated by the Cl- concentration.
